title: Luu-2025-wearable-10.1016/j.brs.2025.06.004
description: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings from the ventral intermediate nucleus (VIM) of the thalamus in 9 adults with medication-refractory essential tremor undergoing deep brain stimulation surgery. At each recording depth, 60 s were recorded without and with transcutaneous afferent patterned stimulation (TAPS), a wearable peripheral nerve stimulation therapy, applied to the treated hand. This derivative BIDS repackaging contains the authors' processed, software-filtered signals (48 kHz) stored in BrainVision format, with motion-artifact masks as events.
methods_description: Recordings were acquired with an FHC Guideline 4000 LP+ system at 48 kHz from anterior, center and posterior Ben-gun microelectrodes, each bipolar against a macro contact. For each depth, 60 s trials were recorded with TAPS off and on. The authors' processed signals were low-pass filtered, zero-mean, trimmed to 60 s and converted to BrainVision float32, with artifact-blanking masks provided as events.
